issues.title: Implement in-memory backend and guarded Google sessions
issues.goal: Enforce identity and current access server-side.
issues.description: Implement only identity/session, health and OAuth contract operations using in-memory identity/session/OAuth-state repositories. Bootstrap administrator from configuration, no public signup. Keep client/campaign/daily CRUD for M08 and reporting for M09. Entry prerequisite M06 has independent local QA PASS at aee0377. Frontend source and frozen OpenAPI remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Public GET health and auth/status match maintained contract; missing Google configuration returns configured:false and login start503.
GET /me without valid nonexpired opaque session returns401; disabled/revoked session is rejected on its next request.
Configured Google start generates one-time browser-bound state and nonce; callback rejects missing, mismatched, expired, replayed or cross-browser state before linking identity.
Provider identity verifies signature/issuer/audience/expiry/nonce/email_verified; only approved enabled normalized email can link. Never create unapproved account.
Successful callback rotates server session and sets HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie; HTTPS production Secure behavior configured. Fixed frontend redirect only.
GET /me returns exact User plus X-CSRF-Token; authenticated logout validates token+trusted Origin, revokes session and clears cookie.
Actual isolated provider/session tests run; live Google handshake remains explicitly unverified without credentials. No production test-login route exists.
issues.constraints: Implement only M07 endpoints and minimum in-memory auth repository. No domain CRUD/reporting or SQLite yet. Contract aee0377 frozen unless genuine bug; no provider secrets or bypasses in git. Use isolated test dependency injection rather than production fake identities.

Money columns store integer minor units, input numeric bounds and nonnegative count/version constraints are represented consistently with domain validation.
Archive/version/timestamps and session expiry fields support approved behavior; foreign-key enforcement is enabled and tested on real SQLite connection.

Current memory backend regression continues passing; no SQLite repository activation or frontend integration in M10.

acceptance_criteria: Default application repository is SQL-backed; explicitly selected memory mode remains available for parity tests only as documented.

SQLite unique constraints and transaction atomicity reject duplicate dates, stale versions and invalid mutations without partial state changes.
Server sessions and OAuth state use persisted repositories with expiry/one-time semantics and no plaintext provider credentials.
Run actual server process, write fixture data through authorized API, stop process, restart with identical SQLite file and read same authorized data and report. Record process commands/results.
Run API regression, migration and repository parity tests; no frontend real-API integration until independent M11 QA PASS.
issues.constraints: M11 repository/runtime/restart only. Use M10 Alembic schema, frozen REST contract and safe per-record bounds. No production authentication test bypass; HTTP tests may inject isolated session fixtures with honest labeling. Preserve actual restart evidence, not merely opening a second ORM session.
